instructions: Cut the paneer into 3/4 inch cubes and drop them into a bowl of warm water. Leave them there while you cook so they turn soft.
Roughly chop the onion and the 4 tomatoes. Peel and slice the ginger and peel the 3 garlic cloves. Thinly slice the green chili into a small bowl for the table. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
Heat the 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the 2 cardamom pods, 3/4 tsp cumin seeds, ginger and garlic and stir for about a minute, until the seeds sizzle and it smells toasty.
Add the onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's light golden.

Add the tomatoes, the 12 cashews and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes, then cover and cook over medium low for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes are soft and mushy. If the pan dries out, add a splash of water.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool for 5 minutes. Scrape everything into a blender, hold the lid down with a towel and blend until it's very smooth.
Melt 1 1/2 tbsp of the ghee in the same pan over medium. Add the cinnamon stick and bay leaf and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds.

Turn the heat to low and stir in the 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder, 3/4 tsp garam masala and 3/4 tsp coriander. After about 20 seconds, pour in the blended masala so the spices don't burn.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the masala thickens and comes together. Stir in the 1 1/4 cups peas, 1 1/4 cups water and the last 1/4 tsp salt.
Bring it to a boil, then partly cover the pan and cook over medium for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until the gravy thickens and you can see a little fat shining on top.

Meanwhile, drain the paneer and pat it dry. Heat the other 1/2 tbsp ghee in a nonstick skillet over medium high. Add the paneer in a single layer and fry it without moving for about 3 minutes, until it's golden underneath. Turn the cubes and fry the other side for 2 to 3 minutes.
Crush the 1 tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the gravy. Add the 1 tsp sugar and the paneer and simmer for 2 minutes, until the paneer is hot through.
Take the pan off the heat. Fish out the cinnamon stick and bay leaf, stir in the 1/4 cup cream and scatter over the cilantro.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve with basmati rice or naan, with the sliced green chili on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions cook onion, tomato and cashews with ginger and garlic, blend them into a smooth masala, cook it again with Kashmiri chili, turmeric and coriander, then simmer peas and paneer in it with water and finish with kasuri methi. Swasthi's Recipes (the lead) starts with cardamom and cumin seeds, blooms the ground spices in ghee with cinnamon and bay leaf before the puree goes back in, simmers the peas 10 to 12 minutes, and suggests softening the paneer in warm water and frying it golden. Cook with Manali adds tomato paste and fennel powder, simmers the paneer and peas for just 3 minutes, and finishes with garam masala, cardamom powder and optional cream. This one follows the lead for 4 with a little more paneer and peas, and fries the paneer for the golden edges.
